QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_12

question.text: A company holds a portfolio of equity stocks worth Rs 50 lakhs with a beta of 1.2 relative to NIFTY. How many NIFTY futures contracts should they sell to hedge? (NIFTY at 25,000, lot size 25)

answer.text: About 10 contracts [N = (Vp x beta) / Vi = (50,00,000 x 1.2) / (25,000 x 25) = 60,00,000 / 6,25,000 = 9.6, rounded to about 10]

explanation.text: The Logic: Number of index futures contracts to short = (Portfolio value x Beta) / (Index level x Lot size) = (50,00,000 x 1.2) / (25,000 x 25) = 60,00,000 / 6,25,000 = 9.6, rounded to about 10 contracts. The Trap: 8 contracts ignores beta; 2 contracts uses the wrong lot size; 12 contracts mis-applies the beta adjustment. Note: Beta-based hedging is an approximation — the actual effectiveness depends on how stable the stock-index beta relationship is over the hedge horizon.
